THE CENSUS PIN FILE IS windows/lab/tests/suite/calibration.rs, unprefixed. Everything matching *_calibration.rs is a per-campaign preregistered readout, and there are eleven: burr, reticence, the_mire, the_fare, health, disposition, gathering, hearth_population, branches_family (all under windows/lab), approach_ease (worldgen), coercion (vessel). CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY OPERATOR GREP: a pattern like calibration matching .rs hits all twelve, and anchoring it to windows/lab/ DOES NOT FIX IT -- eight of the eleven campaign readouts live under windows/lab too, so that anchor removes exactly one false positive and keeps eight. Enumerated from the tree, not reasoned. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PREFIX, NOT THE DIRECTORY: anchor on a path separator immediately before the word calibration, which matches the census pins alone; anything with an underscore before it is a campaign readout needing ordinary review rather than census-pin review. WHY THIS IS A VOCABULARY PROBLEM AND NOT A GREP PROBLEM: two concepts share one word. A census pin is a frozen golden the calibration batteries assert against; a campaign readout is a preregistered measurement frozen before its own code. The incumbent took the bare noun, which is backwards -- the specific instrument should have been namespaced and the general shape left free. Same shape The Coercion settled for possess versus dominate, and settled the same way, by counting: the readouts own the suffix eleven to one, so renaming them is the expensive wrong direction. Recorded rather than fixed, because a rename touches eleven files across three crates and the collision is cheap to live with once named.
